topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening section introduces the lecture series, outlines key learning outcomes, and establishes the multidisciplinary relevance of cancer biology.

topics.label: Cellular and developmental origins of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops through accumulated genetic and epigenetic changes that disrupt normal cellular differentiation, tissue architecture, and three-dimensional growth control.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the malignant transition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the histological criteria, anatomical routes, and stepwise tissue changes that distinguish benign lesions from locally invasive and metastatic malignancies.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and clinical pathophysiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the standard naming systems for neoplasms and the pathophysiological mechanisms by which benign and malignant tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Comparative cancer incidence across species and populations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare epidemiological cancer incidence patterns across human demographic groups and diverse multicellular animal taxa.

topics.label: Clinical symptoms and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the principles, histological markers, and practical effectiveness of early detection and organ-specific cancer screening modalities.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical preview
topics.groupedBecause: This closing section summarizes the session's learning objectives and provides housekeeping information for upcoming practicals and lectures.
